subject.title: Feature request: Escalating stall recovery for sub-agents (nudge → kill)

question: Should OpenClaw add default-on subagent tool-inactivity recovery now, and should its thresholds, injected nudge, abort semantics, and user-visible terminal notification live in the core subagent runtime or wait for the broader session-activity/watchdog design?
rationale: The remaining work adds new config/default behavior, automatic kill policy, model-visible injected messages, and channel-visible recovery semantics, so automation cannot choose the product boundary safely.

options.title: Design core subagent recovery
options.body: Keep this issue as the core subagent slice and define guarded defaults, nudge copy, abort semantics, parent/channel notification, docs, and focused tests before implementation.

options.title: Depend on session activity first
options.body: Keep the issue open but make #39127/#39141 prerequisites so nudge/kill consumes one gateway-owned activity and attention source.

options.title: Limit core to hard timeout and manual controls
options.body: Do not add automatic nudge/kill defaults now; rely on runTimeoutSeconds and the separate kill/reap surface if maintainers decide automatic abort is too risky.

recommendation.title: Design core subagent recovery
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the core subagent slice and define guarded defaults, nudge copy, abort semantics, parent/channel notification, docs, and focused tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest merged history across subagent timeout enforcement, terminal outcome precedence, and recovery-sensitive runtime policy in the inspected path.
